recipes.name: Quick and Easy Peach Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 2 (16 ounce) cans sliced peaches in heavy syrup

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Whisk self-rising flour, sugar, and milk together in a bowl until well combined and no lumps remain.
Pour melted butter into a 2-quart baking dish (or a 9- or 10-inch cast-iron skillet); pour flour-milk mixture over top.
Carefully pour peaches and syrup into the skillet; spread peaches evenly around the skillet using a spatula.
Bake in the preheated oven until the crust turns golden brown, 30 to 45 minutes.
Cool cobbler for about 10 minutes to ensure it sets for easy serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick and Easy Peach Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy, 5-ingredient peach cobbler recipe comes together and bakes to sweet perfection in minutes—serve it warm with vanilla ice cream.

video.description: An easy peach cobbler made with just 5 common ingredients you probably always have on hand? That's right! The simple dessert in this video comes together in minutes and bakes to sweet perfection in a cast iron skillet. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream and whipped cream.

review.reviewBody:
I have been making this recipe for years. My Swede-heart loves it. 
Only thing I have changed was adding 1/4tsp nutmeg and 1/2 tsp cinnamon to the flour mixture. Comes out perfect everytime!

I have made this several times and it is a big hit w/ my husband. Just two of us, so I use an 8x8 dish and only one can of peaches and only about 2/3 of the butter. However, I make the batter as indicated. Adding a liberal 1/2 tsp of cinnamon and 1/4 tsp of nutmeg is a must. As someone else suggested, I put the butter and peaches on the bottom and pour the batter over. FYI: The batter will be VERY thin and you'll think it won't work, but it does. I don't buy self-rising flour, so I also add 1.5 tsp of baking powder and 1/4 tsp of salt to the flour. I don't think you'll be disappointed in this quick cobbler w/ canned peaches, when you fresh ones are out of season.

I did what other reviews said and added baking powder to all-purpose flour instead of using self rising & also added the cinnamon & nutmeg. I did half dark brown & half granulated sugar...Just the southern girl in me that thinks brown sugar belongs in cobbler, I suppose. Took the advice of another reviewer & drained 2 of the cans of peaches, too. Definitely would've been too soupy if I hadn't! Mixed all the ingredients together & poured them over the peaches the pan. I baked mine in a 12" cast iron skillet so I doubled the recipe, though most, but not all of the topping would fit in the pan, for I had to leave room for rising. Had to bake at 375 at the end & for longer than time recommend for it to finish cooking through, probably due to the cast iron or the doubled recipe. Everyone thought it was delicious, and it came out a little gooey and not too sweet. Just the way you'd want a peach cobbler to be! This is a keeper for for my recipe book now!

It is a basic recipe that you can make your own by adding the flavors you want. I used 1/8 tsp of almond extract and 1 tsp vanilla extract. I used 1/2 C brown sugar, 1/2 C white sugar, the recipe says to use 1/2 C of butter (not 1/2 of a stick); I have AP flour, so yes I added 2 tsp of baking powder, and 1 tsp of salt, and 1 tsp of cinnamon. I left it in the oven for 50 min to get the golden brown color, and we love the chewy edges that are a brownie consistency.

This is our go-to recipe when we crave something sweet in the evenings. I can make it during a commercial! I melt a stick of butter in my casserole dish in the oven while I mix the flour, sugar, and milk. Then I pour the batter on top of the butter and carefully pour the can of peaches on top of the batter. That's it! No stirring, so the batter rises evenly across the top as it bakes. Adjusted for my family's taste we use a little less sugar and only one can of peaches. I can work much harder and not please them as much!

Use all the same measurements but add one can of pears. First mix all ingredients except for the peaches and pears together. THEN put the peaches AND pears in the pan First and add the batter On Top. Bakes perfect every time and the pears add an amazing extra flavor. (Cobbler with just the peaches can get a little one-note for me)

I added 1/2 teaspoon of Cinnamon and a shake of ginger like it was suggested in the other reviews. To make it sugar-free, I added 1/4 cup of monk fruit sweetener to one half of the recipe and sugar to the other to make two cobblers, both were really good. I decreased the sugar to about 1/4 cup and it was still really good. I also didn't put any syrup from the peaches in because there was added sugar and it would make the cobbler soggy like some other people were saying.

I made this tonight! The picture doesn’t do it justice. I added some extras though. I used a large can of the DelMonte peaches. I believe it was 29oz. I also added a 1/4 cup of sugar. 1-1/2 tablespoons of cinnamon to the batter. I used salted butter. Oh the flavor was incredible. After I added the peaches I skirted some lemon juice on the peaches. Before putting it in the oven, I topped it with a few sprinkles of Brown Sugar. I did bake it for about an hour and let it sit for 10 minutes. The buttery crust and sweet and tartness of the peaches complemented one another well. I want to eat the whole pan.
Very easy and flexible - I did use fresh peaches and a 1/2 cup of brown sugar mixed with 1/2 cup of white sugar - I also added about 3/4 c of fresh blueberries and sprinkled cinnamon on top
Actually substituted a can of condensed milk and 1/2 cup whole milk, plus reduced sugar to 1/2 cup. Then added 1 qt. Sliced fresh peaches ( cause we gave a tree). It worked wonderfully!!
I sprinkled in some cinnamon and nutmeg in the flour and milk mixture. 1/8 of a teaspoon of each. once baked, I sprinkled cinnamon sugar over the top.
Simple, easy, tasty. I used fresh peaches and cut the sugar in half with allulose. Yummy 😋

I kid you not...this recipe rocks! I never made a peach cobbler with these ingredients, but I followed the recipe, reduced the sugar, and I used fresh peaches and nectarines since they were getting very ripe. This had the best taste, and with vanilla ice cream its a true winner.
This was great and, oh, so, simple. Cobblers should be simple.
Tried it last night everyone loved it outstanding
On Only used half the juice.
The first time making this it was a major hit.
I added a little cinnamon, nutmeg and bout 1/2 tsp of almond extract! BIG HIT! Definitely a keeper!

I substituted Splenda for the sugar. Had to increase to 3 cups. I also used water packed peaches. I thickened it with Xanthan gum & it helped the consistency. My family loved it! I just made it a little bit more diabetic friendly. This is my"go to" recipe for ALL of my cobblers!! LOVE IT!!!

Too soupy even after draining all of the juice and needed more time in the oven. Maybe another 15 minutes. Not sure if it was my oven or not. I will try again with less milk and maybe a tsp of corn starch to thicken.
